scenes.line1: Why use forests, not just one tree?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why we build forests of trees in machine learning instead of just one?

scenes.label: Tree
scenes.sub: Splits data by feature values for predictions.
scenes.say: A decision tree splits data by feature values to make predictions. Simple, powerful, but can overfit.
Random forests grow lots of independent trees and average their results. Gradient boosting builds trees one after another, each learning from the last one's mistakes.

scenes.title: Random Forest in scikit-learn
scenes.say: In scikit-learn, you can train a random forest by setting the number of trees. Here, one hundred trees are averaged for a strong prediction.

scenes.question: Can you ignore tuning tree depth?
scenes.right: No, tuning depth and estimators balances bias and variance.
scenes.say: Don't skip tuning tree depth or the number of trees. These settings help balance bias and variance for better results.
